blurb: Joo Chiat Road has one of Singapore's best stretches of independent shops. Start north, dig your way south.

stops.note: 1950s to 90s pieces, plus the pay-by-weight Kilo Tale corner.
More vintage racks.
Crate-dig, then pizza for lunch.

title: Rainy day mall crawl
blurb: When the sky opens, Katong's two malls are a short covered dash apart. Everything here is indoors.

stops.note: UNIQLO, MANGO, KKV and the beauty counters on level 1.
lululemon and Typo on level 1.
Indoor climbing on level 4. No experience needed.
Movie on level 5.
Chocolate cake across the road. Open late.

title: Peranakan heritage afternoon
blurb: Katong was the heartland of the Straits Chinese. Eat and tour your way through the culture that painted these streets.

stops.note: Nyonya dumplings and kueh. See the kebaya boutique upstairs.
Spoon-only laksa for lunch.
Baba-Nyonya antiques. Call ahead.
Home museum tour with tea. Appointment only.
See the real houses in late light.
Dinner at Singapore's oldest Peranakan restaurant.

title: The laksa showdown
vibe: Two bowls, one verdict, gelato after
blurb: Two famous laksa shops face each other across East Coast Road and each claims the crown. Try both and settle it.

stops.note: The self-declared original, in Roxy Square. Closes 4:30pm.
The one that beat Gordon Ramsay.
The 1925 bakery landmark.
Gelato to cool down.
Coffee and the final verdict.

title: Golden hour at East Coast Park
blurb: Rent bikes, ride east with the sea on your right, watch the sky turn from the jetty and end at Singapore's only beachside hawker centre.

stops.note: Coffee at Marine Cove before you ride.
Rent bikes nearby and head east.
Stop to watch the wakeboarders.
Sunset is around 7pm all year.
Satay and BBQ stingray by the beach.
